recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No follow-up source work is needed unless the Structured Documents work group opens a new tracker to revise the broader wording about context flow versus references.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive Structured Documents change request asking to add Composition wording that, unlike CDA, FHIR document context applies to the Composition itself and not specifically to contained or referenced resources; each resource expresses its own context to support safe extraction.
initial_application: Git-svn commit 7612479cd11d1208dd4461ea4be3a94f7c667716 added the Composition note with subject '#6919 - add note to composition about context conduction not existing in FHIR' and records build@6189, matching the Jira comment 'svn revision 6189'.
additional_context: Composition is an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini and assigned to Structured Documents. Later editorial changes preserved the no-context-flow rule; FHIR-30766 removed confidentiality from the parenthetical, consistent with current Composition having no Composition.confidentiality element and the CDA comparison now mapping confidentiality to Bundle.meta.security. Jira FHIR-7105 is a duplicate of the same request, and a later Zulip discussion supports the distinction between explicit references and context flow without requiring a source change.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/composition/composition-introduction.xml already carries the semantic rule requested by FHIR-6919 in current build scope.

related_jiras.note: Duplicate tracker with identical proposed wording and comment 'Tracker 6919'; recorded as related but not independently decided.
Later CDA wording update removed confidentiality from the FHIR-6919 parenthetical, consistent with current Composition structure.

evidence_items.learned: This later community discussion supports the current Composition rule and does not identify a conflicting source change.
